title: Monads and Distributive Laws in Substructural Contexts (Extended Version)
summary: We present a categorical theory of monads and distributive laws in substructural contexts. In the study of distributive laws, the roles of (the absence of) structural rules for variable contexts have been recognized; our theory formalizes these substructural situations using Tronin's verbal categories $\mathbf W$, in a uniform and presentation-independent manner. We introduce the classes of $\mathbf W$-operadic monads (those defined via the structural rules in $\mathbf W$) and of $\mathbf W$-commutative monads (those invariant under the structural rules in $\mathbf W$).
